blockers: §3.4 attest_outcome + §9 G3 test path: G3 says 'test-only relayer run against an already-settled event WXHIGH-AUS-2611170459'. But attest_outcome requires resolved_at >= sales_close_ts, and create_promise requires now < sales_close_ts. That event resolved 2026-11-17T11:02Z, so the attestation always reverts TooEarly. The G3 end-to-end loop (and the 3x e2e-devnet.ts rehearsal in §10.2) cannot pass on devnet as specified. You need a test-only feature build, a local validator with clock warp, or a fresh event that settles before H19. In practice that is the Nov-18 Austin high (WXHIGH-AUS-2611190459), which settles around Thu 05:02 CST = H16. Create a promise on it tonight with sales_close before its resolution.

§5.2 tranche rule vs §7.1/§7.3 hero: with topup_threshold = 0, rule (a) `hedged_capacity - sold <= topup_threshold` fires as soon as receipt #10 is issued (10-10 = 0 <= 0). The agent also runs 'on timer'. So it pre-buys the next tranche before the third judge scans, and receipt #11 never bounces Unhedged. The hero (D2) is broken by its own config. The threshold must be 'disabled' (e.g. -1, or null meaning revert-triggered only), not 0.

§5.2 price-ceiling guard vs §4.1 weather pair: limit_i = ask_i + 0.02. For the '74F or warmer' strip that is 0.55 + 0.13 + 0.03 = 0.71 > PRICE_CEILING 0.70, so the guard aborts and the hot-drinks promise of Run #1 never hedges at Wednesday's prices. Use a per-strip ceiling on Σask, not Σ(ask + slippage), or raise the ceiling for multi-bin strips.

§3.4 refund_crank/release: one customer can permanently lock the merchant's vault. The customer holds their browser key and can close their (empty) USDC ATA, pocketing the 0.00204 SOL rent the merchant paid. Then (a) every crank batch containing that receipt fails as a whole (the transfer to a closed holder_ata fails), and (b) release on SETTLED_YES requires refunded == sold, with no timeout escape. The vault is stuck forever. Fix: the crank should skip or create the missing ATA (init_if_needed paid by cranker/vault), or pay to a receipt-PDA escrow. Add a 'refunded == sold OR now > resolved_at + N days' release path.

§5.9/§6.3/§6.4 + §2 hosting: a Cloudflare quick tunnel gets a new random hostname on every restart. PUBLIC_URL is baked into the counter QR and the customer backup links (`/w#sk=`). The customer keypair lives in localStorage scoped to that origin. If the tunnel restarts between Thu 9 AM (Run #1 sales) and the Fri 5 AM payout, every Run #1 customer loses access to their '$1 is yours' page and the video's payout beat breaks. A named tunnel or stable domain (U6) must be mandatory, not optional, before Run #1.

§3.4 issue_receipt seeds use promise.sold. Two concurrent scans (the hero has 'two judges scan' at once) derive the same receipt PDA, so the second tx fails with a raw 'account already in use' (system program error 0x0), not one of the mapped 6000-6015 codes. /api/receipts must serialize issuance per promise (a queue/mutex) and map unknown errors. Otherwise judge #2 sees a generic failure on stage.

§4.2/§9 G1: everything the Gemini bounty and the hero rest on is still unverified until the user's KYC'd account has Predictions API trading on production: Trader-role keys, /order/batch, fills, fees, USD funding without an ACH hold on trading. The NO-GO switch is at H4 (5 PM Wed today). U1/U2 (fund ≥ $75, create keys) are user-only and must happen in the next ~3 hours or the whole plan pivots.

§4.4 fallback 'USDC_MINT=self (existing `npm run setup`)': package.json points `setup` at scripts/setup.ts, but /root/blockchainHackathon26/scripts/ is empty. The fallback does not exist yet. If faucet.circle.com caps cannot deliver ≥ $100 (U4) by Run #1, there is no ready mint script.
holes: Receipts are not tied to a purchase (§1 step 3, §6.3). Anyone who sees or photographs the rotating counter QR, or scripts the code-polling endpoint behind /counter/[id], can mint receipts to fresh keypairs until cap. Each costs the merchant about 0.004 SOL of rent plus a $1 liability. Nothing gates issuance on a sale (no cashier tap or POS step). This also contradicts H5's 'every customer pays the normal price': free entry vs purchase-required changes the legal analysis (Texas lottery = prize + chance + consideration).

§5.8 cosign allowlist allows amount <= balance, which includes 0. It also allows createAssociatedTokenAccountIdempotent for any destination paid by the merchant. An attacker can create keypairs plus one ATA each (self-funded), then send 5 zero-amount cash-outs per key per hour to fresh destinations. Each one costs the merchant 0.002 SOL of ATA rent plus fees, a 5:1 drain ratio. Require amount > 0, a source ATA that is a receipt holder_ata, and a global rate limit.

Rent economics (§3.2): the 0.00193 SOL receipt PDA rent is never reclaimed (there is no close instruction among the 6), and the 0.00204 SOL customer ATA rent goes to the customer. At the pitched 300-cover night that is about 1.2 SOL/night of merchant cost, the same order as the $217.50 premium at mainnet SOL prices. This undercuts the D6 'only cost is the premium' line. Add a close_receipt (rent back to merchant after refund/settle) or use compressed receipts or events.

§3.4 attest_hedge CUTOFF counters update 'on the first CUTOFF only', but §7.3 Run #2 does a sell-back after tip-off and then a CUTOFF re-attest showing 90%. The first CUTOFF at sales_close+30s already recorded 100% and incremented cutoff_held_full. So the onchain track record says 'held full' while the receipt badge says 'Hedge reduced'. The recorded clip showcases an inconsistency in the D4 track record.

D4 'gate is not cosmetic' is weak: the merchant can sell its entire Gemini position one minute after CUTOFF (PRESETTLE is #2 on the cut list), and the track record never sees it. The positions belong to the merchant's own Gemini account, which can also be traded manually in the web UI. A judge can rightly say the hedge is attested at one instant and is otherwise unenforced.

orders_hash (§3.2, §3.6 mitigation 'order ids are hashed onchain') can't be checked by any third party. Gemini order ids and positions are private to the account, so no customer or judge can reproduce the preimage. As a mitigation for attestor over-reporting it is decorative. Say so, or publish the order ids plus fills in terms.json and /p/.

Trust table §3.6 says the attestor 'cannot move funds', but key B is a Trader-role key on the merchant's Gemini account. It can place and cancel orders (buy or sell hedges) and is only 'read-only by code path'. Judges from Gemini will notice the role semantics.

Cancelled/postponed games: §3.4 attest_outcome says 'a postponed game resolves NO'. The live Clippers contract text (fetched 2026-11-18) instead says: 'If the Expiration Value cannot be determined... (including because the event is cancelled...) the Exchange may determine payouts pursuant to the Market Outcome Review Process'. Resolution can be delayed or non-binary. Meanwhile the relayer gives up at +48h and the program's 72h timeout pays customers YES (D9), even if Gemini later resolves NO. The merchant then pays refunds and also loses its hedge, so D9 is a merchant-side economic hole on postponements.

No cancel path: if the hedge fails (HEDGE_FAILED, capacity 0, sold 0), the merchant's cap × $1 stays locked until the relayer settles the event or until expected_resolve + 72h. A create-time demo failure strands the vault USDC you're already short of (U4 faucet limits). Allow release when sold == 0 at any time.

refund_crank/release account constraints are unspecified for `merchant`. If they are not constrained to seeds ['merchant', promise.merchant], a cranker can pass any merchant PDA and inflate or deflate another merchant's refunds_paid and promises_closed counters, which pollutes the 'track record' that D4 sells.
§3.4 per_bin_capacity = qty_centi[i] (u32) × 10_000: this overflows u32 once qty_centi > 429,496 (≈4,295 contracts, e.g. cap 500 × $10 refund). Cast to u64 before multiplying.

Verify widget §6.5 re-hashes the event and checks that the receipt's contract is in the strip. It does not assert that Gemini's yes-contract ∈ strip ⇔ onchain status == SETTLED_YES. A relayer that posts the correct canonical hash with winning_symbol = '' (a false NO, the exact threat in §3.6) passes the hash tick. Add an explicit 'Gemini outcome vs onchain outcome' tick.

Hero latency (§7.1 2:00-2:50): revert detected → book fetch → batch IOC → key-B positions read (Gemini position-update latency unverified) → order-history read → attest tx confirmed on devnet → retry issue, all inside the phone's 30 s retry window. Devnet confirmation often takes 5-20 s under load. The rehearsal target is <20 s with no measured number yet. Pre-warm the blockhash and have the agent trigger the attestor directly with fill quantities.

Run #2 sell-back 'after tip-off' (§7.3) assumes Gemini PM keeps NBA contracts tradeable in-play with a bid. That is unverified: marketState may switch at startTime and in-play books may be empty. The hedge-reduced clip (D3) depends on it. Do the sell-back just before tip-off instead.

The legal framing H5 ('uniform purchase rebate') holds under Texas Penal Code ch. 47 even though receipts in this design need no purchase, and a regulated exchange's sponsor judges are comfortable with sports-outcome promos aimed at bar customers.
judge_questions: The vault already holds 100% of the payout, so the customer is safe without any hedge. What does Gemini add for the customer? And if it is only the merchant's P&L, why does the merchant need to post 100% collateral on Solana and also buy contracts at Gemini, whose YES payout lands in USD in a different venue? (Capital is roughly doubled, and the D6 'deposit not a cost' line ignores that the Gemini payout is not in the vault.)

Who runs the attestor and relayer in your demo? (Answer: you, the same team that is the merchant.) Gemini order ids are private, so how can anyone outside your team check that the hedge you attested exists, and what stops the merchant from selling the hedge one minute after cutoff?

Your counter QR gives a $1 claim to anyone who scans it, with no purchase check. What stops a table of students from minting all 20 receipts? And if a purchase is required, isn't a purchase plus a chance-based prize a lottery in Texas, not a 'uniform rebate'?

What happens when a game is postponed or cancelled? Gemini's own rules send that to a 'Market Outcome Review Process', but your program pays customers YES after 72 hours. Who eats the loss, and what if Gemini resolves after your timeout?

At 300 covers a night, what does the merchant actually pay all-in: premium, Gemini fees, spread (the weather pair costs $1.10 per paired $1), plus about 0.004 SOL of unrecoverable rent per receipt? And how many real bars will lock $1,500 every game night? Have you talked to a single real merchant? (Q5 in §11 says no.)
